[[File:Scorpiurus muricatus MHNT.BOT.2007.43.42.jpg|thumb|''Scorpiurus muricatus'' - [[MHNT]]]]

'''''Scorpiurus muricatus''''', the '''caterpillar-plant'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''prickly scorpion's-tail''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SCMU3|taxon=Scorpiurus muricatus|accessdate=8 November 2015}}</ref> is an [[Annual plant|annual]] [[leguminous]] plant native to southern Europe and the [[Syria (region)|region of Syria]] with tiny pea-like flowers and [[Leaf shape|simple leaves]] uncharacteristic of a [[legume]].  Its contorted, pubescent pods give rise to its common name "prickly caterpillar".  Extracts of the species have been found to have [[allelopathic]] effects on  [[microbes]] of the genus ''[[Fusarium]]'' due to the high concentration of [[phytoalexin]]s in the plants' tissues.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q111370060}}</ref>

This is mainly a garden plant used as a [[groundcover]].  Its densely haired pods may be added to salads for interest, and its leaves used as a salad herb in some Mediterranean countries.
